Point-in-time inventory and container views, and three logging fixes for events that were recorded wrongly or not at all.

- New /sg snapshot: reconstruct a player inventory or a container as it stood at a past instant, browse it in a GUI, and take items back out of it. Every take is logged and attributed, so pulling an item out of a reconstructed inventory is itself searchable history.
- FastAsyncWorldEdit edits are logged correctly again on FAWE 2.15.2. On that version Spyglass took its notes after FAWE had already written the chunk, so it read the new blocks as the "before" state and logged every placed block as a break of the material that had just been placed. Generation commands and brushes (//cyl, //pyramid, //sphere) lost their place records entirely, and //paste and //move gained phantom breaks at the destination. Logging now happens in the stage where the before and after data are both valid. FAWE 2.15.0 and earlier were never affected. Records already written by an affected build cannot be repaired, because the "placed" facts were never stored.
- Hopper, dropper and dispenser movement is recorded per slot, each record carrying that slot's exact contents before and after. A container snapshot now replays automated traffic exactly, instead of returning a confident wrong answer for a container a hopper had drained. These records are still never touched by rollback or restore. Every movement is now recorded rather than one per flow window, so servers running heavy hopper farms should watch disk and reach for the per-event toggles or a shorter per-event retention.
- Container access on animals and chest boats is logged. Horse saddle and armor slots, donkey, mule and llama chests, and chest boats produced no records at all: no deposits, no withdrawals, and no open or close pair. Minecart inventories now also emit open and close records, which the old code dropped.
- /sg version shows the support Discord.

Config upgrades from v2 to v3 on first boot and your existing file is backed up beside it. The two hopper transfer events changed names, and the migration carries any toggle or retention you had set on the old names across to the new ones. Stored data is unchanged and no data migration runs, so upgrading is a jar swap.
